label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Rohan, fair question da. You trusted me with real money, and you deserve a straight answer—not a LinkedIn caption.

We let 6 of 14 people go last Friday. I gave everyone two months’ pay, and we’ve already helped four get interviews. It was the worst day of my life—worse than failing maths in second sem, which I thought was my personal rock bottom.

The bridge round from the Hyderabad fund fell through on 28 October, when the term sheet was basically ready. Their partner said “we love the energy,” then went quiet for 11 days. So: not exactly a masterclass in communication.

After the cuts, we have about five months of runway. The app has around 41,000 monthly users. Plumbers and electricians are growing; AC servicing is losing money, so we’re planning to shut that down and focus on housing-society tie-ups. We’ve signed pilots with three societies in HSR. I think there’s a real shot there, but it’s not a sure thing.

So the honest answer on your and Divya’s ₹3 lakh: it’s still invested on the same terms as everyone else in the 2025 friends round. The money is at risk. I can’t tell you it’s safe, and I don’t know how this ends—but it isn’t gone. I won’t pretend to know more than I do.

Can I call you both properly this week and walk you through the numbers? You’re absolutely entitled to ask, and I should have told you directly rather than leaving you to decode my terrible LinkedIn prose.

And yes, I’m okay. The office Maggi situation is now so regular that the security uncle asks whether I want masala or plain. Amma also asked if TCS is still hiring, so the family morale dashboard is… mixed.

I’m coming Saturday. Pranav is buying. For the record, I’m not asking anyone to pretend things are rosy—just not to start practising the sad face before we’ve had dosa.
